lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The résumé lacks a concise summary or research-focus line stating the intended quantitative role.
items.because: Recruiters currently must infer the target profile from the experience section.

items.says: The résumé lacks a dedicated publications or selected research section.
items.because: The JASA submission, working paper, research software, and presentations are scattered and understate the research profile.

items.says: The section order gives the bakery role too much visual status relative to quantitative research.
items.because: The strongest evidence should dominate the first page.

items.says: The Northpeak bullets should lead with the verified signal result and validation methodology.
items.because: The current order delays the strongest evidence, and hiring managers may read only the first two bullets.

items.says: The overlaps among the Ph.D., internship, bakery employment, and independent research need clearer categorization.
items.because: Recruiters may otherwise question continuity, availability, and whether projects were academic, personal, or professional.

items.says: The code link should be a complete, clickable URL.
items.because: Recruiters should be able to verify the work without guessing what the link represents.

items.says: The placeholder domain should be replaced if it is not merely anonymized for the review.
A complete and consistent LinkedIn profile could be added.
A location or relevant “open to” indication could be added.
The Ph.D. entry should add a relevant research area, dissertation topic, advisor, or specialization.
items.because: “Ph.D. candidate in Statistics” does not show whether the work is relevant to markets, forecasting, statistical learning, or computational research.

items.says: The expected completion date should be included only if it is reliable.
Relevant graduate coursework could be added if it fills an obvious gap.
items.because: Coursework such as financial econometrics, stochastic processes, optimization, or machine learning could establish missing role relevance.

items.says: The entry should clarify availability for full-time employment before May 2026.
The B.S. entry should receive less visual weight than the Ph.D.
items.because: The undergraduate degree is no longer a major differentiator given the doctoral work.

items.says: Meaningful honors, awards, or a relevant concentration could be added.
The bakery role may not belong on a targeted quant résumé and should be shortened if retained.
items.because: It is not directly relevant to quantitative research and may make recruiters question continued quantitative engagement.

items.says: The bakery entry should more clearly contextualize its time period alongside the Ph.D. and internship.
items.because: Its current placement may create questions about continuity in quantitative work.

items.says: The management bullet should not take more space than necessary on a quant résumé.
items.because: Management and operational discipline are secondary to research, backtesting, and software experience for the target roles.

items.says: The 12%-to-7% figures should be verified as consistently calculated.
The bullet should explain the measurement period and causal contribution to the reduction in unsold bread.
items.because: The current wording attributes the operational improvement without that context.

items.says: The inventory metric is low priority for a trading or quantitative-research application.
items.because: It does not establish quant-research capability.

items.says: “Risk-adjusted returns” should be defined as Sharpe, information ratio, return per unit of volatility, or another specific measure.
items.because: The phrase is too broad for a quantitative audience.

items.says: The bullet should specify the evaluation period, baseline, and whether the 35% improvement was out of sample.
items.because: Otherwise it sounds like an unqualified performance claim.

items.says: The bullet should explain whether the smoother changed turnover, transaction costs, drawdown, capacity, or Sharpe.
items.because: Its operational effect is currently unclear.

items.says: “Position smoother” should be explained.
items.because: The term is left unexplained for the reader.

items.says: The 35% result should be verified as distinct from the later Sharpe improvement.
items.because: It may describe the same performance result claimed elsewhere in the Northpeak entry.

items.says: The validation bullet should state whether transaction costs, market impact, and latency were included.
items.because: Those details determine the credibility of a financial backtest.

items.says: The bullet should clarify whether the six years covered multiple market regimes.
Purged splits and an embargo do not establish that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: They reduce leakage but do not guarantee freedom from look-ahead or selection bias.

items.says: The feature-store bullet should name relevant implementation technologies.
items.because: The current statement does not show the engineering difficulty.

items.says: The bullet should clarify whether the work covered the data model, ingestion, validation checks, or only joining logic.
items.because: The scope of the engineering contribution is unclear.

items.says: The feature-store impact should quantify reliability, time saved, or reduced repeated preparation if possible.
items.because: Reuse alone does not fully communicate the business or engineering impact.

items.says: The allocation status should distinguish approval, scheduling, deployment, and launch.
items.because: Approval and actual deployment are materially different to a technical reviewer.

items.says: The bullet should state whether live performance, risk, turnover, or post-deployment behavior was monitored.
The wording should not imply that portfolio-manager approval proves the signal worked.
items.because: Approval shows an investment decision, not successful performance.

items.says: The best Sharpe from 400 backtested configurations cannot be reported as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Treating a post-selection maximum as expected live performance is classic selection bias.

items.says: The parameter-selection claim conflicts with the résumé’s otherwise careful leakage and walk-forward-validation claims.
items.because: It makes the methodology appear trustworthy only in some parts of the process.

items.says: The order-book result appears duplicated in the Kaggle entry and must be consolidated or clearly distinguished.
items.because: Both claims use order-book imbalance, futures, 18 months, and a 0.4 Sharpe increase.

items.says: “Out-of-sample” should be confirmed as accurate after all tuning and selection.
items.because: Post-selection testing can invalidate an out-of-sample characterization.

items.says: The bullet should clarify whether the result was an incremental signal, a standalone strategy, or an improvement to the entire desk book.
items.because: The scope of the claimed Sharpe change is unclear.

items.says: “After costs” should specify whether realistic transaction costs and market impact were included.
items.because: The result requires especially careful evaluation detail.

items.says: The ownership and provenance of the signal should be made unambiguous.
items.because: The similar Kaggle claim creates a credibility problem about where the work was performed.

items.says: Running every Monte Carlo worker with the same random seed can produce duplicated or correlated simulations.
items.because: Parallel Monte Carlo generally requires independent random streams or independently assigned seeds to preserve validity.

items.says: The JASA paper should be surfaced in a publications or selected research section.
items.because: The research credential is currently buried in the experience section.

items.says: The entry should identify the candidate’s authorship position.
The paper’s status should precisely distinguish under review, submitted, and published.
items.because: Publication status must be transparent.

items.says: The result’s relevance to high-dimensional statistics or statistical learning should be explained.
The wording should not imply that journal acceptance has already occurred.
items.because: A paper under review is not yet published or accepted.

items.says: The teaching bullet should appear below the research and software contributions.
items.because: Teaching is secondary for most industry quant roles.

items.says: The teaching detail could be shortened or omitted if space is limited.
items.because: It should not compete with research, backtesting, or software experience.

items.says: The R package should include its name and repository link.
items.because: That would make the software output verifiable.

items.says: The meaning of 3,000 downloads should be clarified as package downloads, repository clones, or another metric.
Documentation, testing, or external contributors could be mentioned if meaningful.
The R package should receive greater prominence instead of being hidden among ordinary research-assistant bullets.
items.because: It is a differentiating combination of statistical methods, software delivery, and external adoption.

items.says: The volatility result should state the forecast horizon.
items.because: Financial forecasting results are highly sensitive to horizon.

items.says: The bullet should explain how training, validation, and test periods were separated.
items.because: The credibility of the out-of-sample result depends on split design.

items.says: The bullet should explain whether hyperparameter selection occurred inside the training process.
items.because: Financial forecasting results are sensitive to selection leakage.

items.says: The bullet should state whether the 30 indices were modeled separately or jointly.
items.because: The current wording leaves possible cross-sectional leakage and model scope unclear.

items.says: The two crisis periods should be explicitly defined.
items.because: Without definitions, the claim may look selected after observing the results.

items.says: The Diebold-Mariano test assumptions and dependence structure should be shown as appropriately handled.
The bullet should distinguish statistical significance from economic significance.
The volatility working paper should be moved to a research or publications section if it is important.
items.because: Its current placement makes the research output look like an afterthought.

items.says: The working paper’s status should be presented consistently with the JASA paper.
The seminar presentation should be subordinate to the research result.
items.because: The research result is more important than the presentation venue.

items.says: The Kaggle title should be verified and changed if the work was not actually part of that competition.
items.because: The bullets sound like institutional trading research, creating a provenance problem.

items.says: The competition bullet should add a meaningful outcome, rank, or dataset scale.
items.because: It does not currently show whether the project was successful.

items.says: The description is too generic to establish a distinctive technical challenge.
items.because: Feature engineering and gradient boosting alone do not differentiate the project.

items.says: The bullet should explain the exact temporal grouping and whether purging or embargoing was necessary.
items.because: The leakage correction is not fully specified.

items.says: It should be verified that closing the leaderboard gap reflected improved generalization rather than merely matching the leaderboard more closely.
items.because: A closer validation estimate does not itself prove a better model.

items.says: The bullet needs a competition result or another success metric beyond closing the validation gap.
items.because: “Closed the gap” alone is not a success metric.

items.says: The Sharpe claim appears to duplicate the Northpeak order-book result and should not remain in both places unless clearly distinct.
items.because: The matching methodology, asset class, test length, and 0.4 Sharpe increase create an internal consistency problem.

items.says: The programming list should add supported tools such as version control, SQL, Linux, numerical libraries, data-processing tools, or cloud/HPC tools.
items.because: The experience shows more technical capability than the skills section communicates.

items.says: The programming tools should be organized by relevance to the target role.
Kafka should not be listed unless its use can be explained from meaningful pipeline experience.
items.because: It is disconnected from the rest of the résumé.

items.says: Important package or code repositories should be listed separately.
“Econometircs” is misspelled and should be “econometrics.”
items.because: A spelling error in a core domain term can hurt ATS matching and reduce polish.

items.says: The methods list should use consistent capitalization and punctuation.

The methods list omits demonstrated capabilities such as volatility modeling, financial backtesting, purged validation, point-in-time data handling, multiple-testing correction, Monte Carlo simulation, covariance estimation, and microstructure modeling.
items.because: The current section understates the résumé’s strongest specialized capabilities.

items.says: Relevant truthful terms such as statistical arbitrage, market microstructure, portfolio construction, or risk modeling could be added for ATS coverage.
items.because: Their absence may reduce keyword readiness for quantitative-research roles.

items.says: Statistical methods and financial research methods should be separated if the list becomes long.
